sealed_thresholds.note: registered BEFORE measurement; never tuned to results (Art. XXVII)
sealed_thresholds.ensemble: NONE (single-attacker calibration only; majority-vote ensembles are deferred by the R412 directive)

escalation.reason: measured FPR 1.0 > sealed bar 0.3 (Art. L: the attacker is measured non-selective; its KILL is inadmissible as a terminal verdict and is escalated with the objection preserved)
escalation.rule: the instrument's KILL is measured non-selective (FPR above the sealed bar); the objection is preserved verbatim and ESCALATED for adjudication — the candidate is NOT killed by this attack alone (Art. L); the deterministic gates are unchanged

preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism focuses on rubber-filler interaction and crosslink network rigidity, but completely fails to address the primary failure modes of creep and ozone-induced cracking which are explicitly stated as the problem. There is no explanation of how these adjustments would mitigate these specific degradation mechanisms.

No boundary conditions are specified, making it impossible to evaluate whether the proposed solution would work under real-world conditions of temperature cycling, UV exposure, chemical exposure, and decades of traffic loading that bridge bearings experience.

The candidate's own evidence includes a paper on "seismic damage index" and "fatigue life analysis" of elastomeric bearings, which contradicts the proposed focus on tensile strength and compression set as the primary metrics. The actual failure modes in the evidence (seismic damage, fatigue) are not addressed by the proposed mechanism.

The candidate claims improved properties but provides no comparison data against current baseline materials. Without showing quantifiable improvement over existing solutions, the proposal offers no advantage over the status quo.

The proposal mentions "adjusting semi efficient vulcanization system" but provides no details on how this would be implemented at scale, what the manufacturing process would be, or how it would be integrated into existing production lines. This vagueness makes implementation impossible.

While the proposal mentions testing tensile properties and compression set, it fails to specify the testing protocols, environmental conditions, or acceptance criteria that would determine success. Without standardized measurement protocols, the results would be ambiguous and uncomparable to industry standards.
